records.name: Hydration onboarding & first-sip flow
records.description: Happy-path onboarding for a hydration tracker. Entry: first-launch onboarding carousel (several illustrated screens). The user taps Get Started → chooses measurement units (oz or ml) → follows a short "Add your first sip" tutorial that demonstrates selecting a beverage (water), opening a cup control, adjusting volume and adding a sip. Next the user is shown a Smart Reminders screen and is asked to enable notifications (native iOS permission). The flow then shows a premium upsell carousel with a prominent "Start my 3-day Free trial" CTA. If the user taps the CTA they see pricing and use Apple Pay to confirm the subscription (loading + success confirmation). Exit point: either the user completes the subscription and is returned to the main hydration dashboard, or (alternatively) the user skips enabling reminders / subscription and lands on the main hydration dashboard with current intake shown. Assumptions: user is on iOS, first-time launch, not signed into any account, has Apple Pay configured. Visual language uses playful animal illustrations and a single prominent CTA on each screen.
records.problem: User task: set up the hydration tracker and record the first drink so the app can start tracking daily hydration. From the user perspective they expect a friendly introduction, to select preferred units, be shown how to add a drink, optionally enable reminders, and to see how subscriptions/premium are presented. From the interface perspective the UI guides the user through: a visual onboarding carousel (brand/goal), a units selection modal, a contextual micro-tutorial (Add your first sip) with an affordance bar of beverage icons, a modal cup controller to set volume and confirm adding a drink, a reminders permission step using a native prompt, and a subscription upsell with feature cards and Apple Pay purchase flow. Result / outcomes: user-perceived outcome — first drink recorded, hydration total updated, optional reminders enabled, and optional subscription started. System-level outcome — local state updated with selected units, intake entry created (volume value), notification permissions state recorded, and (if purchased) in-app subscription activated via App Store billing.

content.description:
Full-screen mobile welcome / onboarding screen on a white canvas (safe-area / iPhone X style). Layout is a single centered vertical column with large illustrative art dominating the middle of the screen and a prominent primary call-to-action anchored near the bottom.

Colors (from provided palette):
- Primary text / dark navy: #2C3541 (used for headline and primary button background)
- Accent yellow: #FBAB15 (used for parts of the llama legs/shorts)
- Accent cyan: #44BCDB (used for socks on the llama)
- Accent pink: #E47D94 (used for small jar icon and belly strip on the llama)
- Background / very light: #FBFBFB (background and the llama body fill)

Background: Solid #FBFBFB (appears almost white). No pattern or gradient.

Top area / status bar: Standard system status indicators at the top (time left, signal/wifi/battery right). Leave ~12–20 px top safe margin to accommodate system status.

Small icon above the headline: A small mason-jar icon (square-ish jar with rounded corners and a lid) centered horizontally. Icon color is pink (#E47D94) with a lighter highlight on the lid. Icon size approx 44–56 px square on a 375 px wide layout. Space below status bar ~28–36 px.

Headline: "Track your intake" centered horizontally directly under the jar icon. Typeface: friendly rounded geometric sans (recommend Nunito / Poppins / Quicksand family). Font weight appears medium/semibold. Approx sizes for 375×812 layout: 34–40 pt (mobile pts) with line-height ~1.1–1.2. Text color: #2C3541. Letter spacing slightly tight (-0.5 to 0). There is comfortable vertical spacing: 12–24 px between jar icon and headline.

Mascot illustration (hero): Large stylized llama illustration centered horizontally and placed below the headline. The llama body is a very light gray / off-white (#FBFBFB or #F3F5F6) so it still reads against the white background by using thin subtle shadow/edge or darker details. The belly strip is pink (#E47D94). The llama's lower wool/shorts are yellow (#FBAB15). Lower legs have a brown band (use #2C3541 or darker desaturated brown) then cyan socks (#44BCDB). The illustration takes up the central vertical real estate roughly from y=140 to y=520 (approx 380 px tall on a 375×812 artboard). The illustration is flat, solid color shapes with minimal stroke. No heavy outline; shapes are soft and rounded. Placement: centered horizontally, comfortable breathing room on all sides.

Primary CTA button: A large pill-shaped button centered near the bottom: background #2C3541, text "GET STARTED" uppercase, white (#FFFFFF), bold (700). Button dimensions approx 260–300 px width, 56–64 px height, corner radius 28–32 px (full-pill). Text font size ~18–20 pt, letter spacing +1.5–2 px for the uppercase CTA. Button includes a subtle drop shadow (soft, rgba(44,53,65,0.18), offset 0 6px 16px) to lift it off the background. There is generous bottom margin from safe-area: button sits about 64–88 px from bottom of screen (safe area included).

Language selector / small control: To the left of the CTA (aligned to the CTA baseline, horizontally left of center) is a small circular flag icon (approx 36 px diameter) with a round flag graphic (US/UK flag or union jack and US combined). Immediately to the right of the flag is a tiny label "EN" in light grey (#9AA3B2 or #BFC9D3), uppercase, weight medium, font-size 12–14 pt. This element behaves like a small button to toggle language. Spacing between flag and the left edge of the CTA is ~18–28 px. The language control sits visually in the bottom-left quadrant and is vertically aligned with the CTA horizontally.

Spacing and alignment summary (375×812 baseline examples):
- Left/right main content margin: 20 px
- Top safe area: 12–20 px
- Jar icon top margin from safe area: 28 px
- Headline top margin from jar icon: 12–18 px
- Mascot top margin from headline: 24–36 px
- CTA bottom margin above safe area: 28–36 px (on-screen it sits above safe area but visually ~64–88 px from bottom edge)

Typography: Use Nunito or Poppins family to match the rounded friendly tone.
- Headline: Nunito SemiBold 36–40 pt, line-height 1.1, color #2C3541
- Body / small labels (language): Nunito Regular/Medium 12–14 pt, color #9AA3B2
- CTA text: Nunito Bold 18–20 pt, color #ffffff, uppercase, tracking +1.5–2 px

Iconography & illustration style: Flat, colorful, playful vector illustration with no complex gradients. Shapes have soft rounded corners and no thin hairline strokes. Use solid fills with small highlights if needed. Colors should match palette provided.

Button / control states & micro-interactions:
- CTA default: fill #2C3541, text white, subtle shadow.
- CTA pressed: scale to 0.98, shadow reduces, background slightly darker (multiply #252A33 or 10% darker).
- Language selector: simple tap target 44 px, on tap shows a compact selection popover.

Accessibility:
- Ensure CTA color contrast: #2C3541 on white meets contrast for large text; CTA white on #2C3541 should meet WCAG for the bold uppercase text size used.
- Touch targets: CTA >= 44x44 px, language selector target >= 44x44 px.
- Provide semantic accessibility labels (e.g., "Get started", "Change language"), and alt text for the illustration.

Animations (recommended):
- Small entrance animation: jar icon pops in with a brief scale animation (0 → 1) eased with cubic-bezier(.2,.9,.2,1) over 360ms.
- Headline fades up from 8 px down with 220–300ms delay after jar.
- Mascot eases in from 0.95 scale and 0 opacity to full visibility over 420ms and then gently bobbles vertically +/- 6–8 px (looping slow 4–6s easing) to add life.
- CTA slides up from bottom with fade (200–300ms) and uses an ease-out curve. On press, CTA scales to 0.98 with 80ms easing.

Notes on production assets:
- Provide mascot as multi-layer SVG (separate fills for body, belly, shorts, socks, legs) to enable potential dynamic color changes.
- Provide jar icon as a separate SVG (44–56 px) that can be reused as a micro-illustration.

Overall style: Friendly, playful onboarding/welcome. Generous white space, bold illustrative mascot, clear single CTA, minimal text. Visual language is rounded, soft, and approachable, aimed at quick conversion into the onboarding flow.

The flag avatar is roughly 36 px diameter with a thin border or none; the “EN” label is small (12–14 pt), uppercase, weight 600, color #A0A5C3.

Color palette (primary & accents):

Easing: cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.9, 0.35, 1) for a playful floaty feel. Some confetti pieces use a very subtle scale/rotate micro-interaction on entrance (0.95→1.05 over 300–400 ms).

The layout is vertically stacked and centered, with the primary call-to-action represented as two large pill buttons inside the modal.

- Muted gray (secondary text and system icons): #9A9A9A
- White / sheet background: #FBFBFB

Typography:

The illustration should be a single-color shape (use a very low-contrast gray, e.g., #D0CFD3 or a 10–15% opacity of #9A9A9A) occupying the middle-to-lower area so the silhouette peeks out above the bottom sheet.
- Status bar at top (time/connection/battery) visible in black/dark gray.

Bottom sheet (modal):
- Full width, anchored to bottom. Top corners heavily rounded: corner radius 28–36px. Background: #FBFBFB (white). Height: about 40–48% of the screen (approx 320–380px on 812px tall screen). Include a small top-left/right padding so content sits comfortably. The sheet floats above background with a subtle top drop shadow (blur 10–18px, rgba(0,0,0,0.08)) to separate it from background.
- The sheet content is vertically centered within the sheet area: top large title "Choose your units", spacer, two stacked pill buttons with consistent vertical gap, then bottom padding.

Buttons (pills):
- Two identical pill buttons stacked vertically, centered horizontally.
- Width: ~70% of screen width (approx 260–270px on 375px wide). Height: 64px. Border-radius: 36px (fully rounded pill).
- Background color: #94EEF6. Text color: #FBFBFB (white). Text weight: 700. Text size: 18–20px. Center text horizontally & vertically.
- Button visual effect: subtle inner highlight (top-left gradient) to give a soft glossy feel; small outer shadow: 0 6px 14px rgba(20,125,140,0.12) to lift from sheet. On press/active: scale to 0.98 and reduce shadow, or darker overlay (rgba(0,0,0,0.06)).

- Top-left: device status (time) and top-right: system icons and a "SKIP" action in small uppercase text (#9A9A9A). The Skip is tappable.
- Headline "Add your first sip" positioned around 22–36% from top, center aligned, with generous top margin from status bar.

Icons & illustration:
- The background silhouette of an animal (llama) is centered horizontally and vertically behind the sheet and headline; it is large, low-contrast, and used as decorative art. It should not compete with text readability.

Spacing & grid:
- Use a single centered column layout. Left and right content paddings ~24–28px on mobile. Vertical spacing: status bar to headline ~32–40px; headline to sheet top ~140–180px (allowing illustration to show); sheet top padding ~24–28px; sheet title to first button ~40–48px.

Motion & animation:
- On entry, animate bottom sheet sliding up from bottom over 320–380ms, easing cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) (smooth ease-out). The background illustration can fade in at 220ms. Buttons use micro-interaction: touch ripple or scale animation 120ms ease-in-out.

Accessibility:

- Provide semantic labels for the two unit options and the Skip action.

Assets to export:
- Large silhouette illustration (single-color vector) sized for background with subtle opacity.
- Pill button style (SVG/rounded rectangle) with states: default, pressed, disabled.
- Typeface files (Poppins or Nunito recommended) with weights 600 and 700.

Recreate notes:

Keep visual weight on the cyan pill buttons and maintain a playful, rounded, friendly look. Preserve the skip action top-right and the system status bar visuals to suggest a mobile-first, iOS-style onboarding screen.

Close control

High-level overview
- A clean, playful mobile dashboard for tracking daily hydration. The screen uses generous white space, rounded shapes and friendly illustrations to create a reassuring, gamified health experience. The visual hierarchy places a large numeric readout at the top center followed by a subtitle, a large illustration (a bear silhouette) that visually fills with "water" to show progress, a horizontal row of five drink-type icons with small circular "+" badges, and a rounded bottom card for "Today's tips" partially peeking up from the bottom (bottom sheet). The status bar (time and system icons) sits in the iOS safe area at the very top.

Style and visual language
- Overall style: Playful, illustrative, soft and friendly; generous whitespace; rounded corners everywhere; minimal text; iconography is flat with subtle shadows; microcopy in all-caps for labels under icons.
- Visual motifs: rounded pill controls, circular badges, soft pastel colors, single large centered mascot illustration used as the primary visual progress indicator.

Color palette (primary & supporting; used colors with suggested hex)
- Cyan / Primary accent (numbers, small controls, water fill): #28B1D8
- Teal / secondary accent (selected pills and UI accents): #28B1D8 (same family as primary) — the top left pill appears slightly more saturated; use #19AFC8 for active states if needed
- Gold accent (micro accents / alternate accents): #DABC0F
- Lavender / very light background accent (subtle illustration/background tints): #D1D1F8
- Deep navy / heading or dark text (used sparingly): #2E244F
- Muted slate (secondary text and labels): #43547C
- Light gray / mascot silhouette background: #F1F3F5 (very pale gray)
- Pink bottom card background: #FFDDE0 (soft pastel pink)
- Badge white and translucent shadows: #FFFFFF with 10-12% black overlay for shadow

Typography
- System suggestion: SF Pro Display / SF Pro Text (iOS native), or a rounded geometric humanist like Nunito or Inter for web prototypes.
- Large numeric headline: 56–72pt (mobile points) weight: 600–700 (semi-bold to bold). Color: #28B1D8. Center aligned.
- Subtitle (Hydration • 7% of your goal): 14–16pt, weight: 400–500 (regular / medium), color: #43547C with reduced opacity (~70%). Letter spacing: 0.2–0.4px.
- Small caps labels under beverage icons: 10–12pt, weight: 600 (semi-bold), uppercase, color: #9EA9B6 (muted gray), letter spacing: 1.0–1.5px.
- Pill label and micro UI text: 12–14pt, weight: 600, color: white on active pill; inactive text in #43547C.
- Bottom card header (“Today's tips”): 16–18pt, weight: 600, color: #8B3B4A (darker pink-red hue matching card iconography) or #2E244F for contrast.

UI elements and shapes
- Top-left day selector: a rounded capsule pill ~56–64px tall by ~110–130px wide with a circular knob on the left showing the numeric day in a small filled circle. The pill uses a teal/cyan fill (#28B1D8) and white text. Subtle drop shadow (RGBA(0,0,0,0.08), y:6px, blur:12px).
- Top-right circular icon: white circular button (~44px) with three wave lines icon (stroke color #2E244F at 70% opacity). Shadow and inset to make it tappable.
- Big numeric readout: centered horizontally under the status bar with vertical spacing ~28–36px from safe area. Uses cyan (#28B1D8). Large baseline to the subtitle below.
- Subtitle: centered under the number with smaller muted text describing % of goal.
- Mascot illustration (bear silhouette): centered large illustration occupying approximately 55–65% of the vertical space between the header and the beverage icons. The mascot background is a pale gray (#F1F3F5) and acts as a container for the visual water fill at the bottom. Outline is soft; no heavy stroke. The visible water fill is a rounded organic shape colored cyan (#28B1D8) that sits at the bottom of the silhouette and should be masked to the silhouette shape.
- Water fill: behaves like a miniature liquid surface with a gently undulating top edge (sine-wave like). Height of fill corresponds to hydration percentage. The color is the same cyan accent (#28B1D8) with a slight darker top edge for depth. Add a subtle inner glow (light above fill) to suggest translucency.
- Beverage selector row: horizontally centered row of five illustrated drink icons (Avatar, Water, Green Tea, Coffee, Juice). Each icon sits in its own circular or rounded tile; below each icon sits an uppercase label in muted gray. Each icon has a small circular "+" badge overlay near the bottom center of the icon (white circle with cyan plus and subtle shadow). Tap targets are large (~56–72px diameter) for comfortable touch.
- Bottom sheet / tips card: a wide rounded rectangle with large corner radius (~24–28px) colored pastel pink (#FFDDE0) with text on top and decorative small icons at the right. It is partially visible (peeking) suggesting it can be dragged up. The card has a slight inner shadow and an outer drop shadow to lift it off the page.

Layout & spacing (measured approximations)
- Single column vertical layout centered horizontally. The screen is split into five vertical bands:
  1) Status area (safe area top) with left pill and right circular action (approx. 44–64px tall)
  2) Numeric readout area (number + subtitle) ~120–160px high
  3) Mascot / progress illustration area (dominant) ~50–60% of remaining height
  4) Beverage row (horizontal selector) ~90–120px
  5) Bottom sheet teaser (rounded card) ~120–140px tall, peeking from bottom
- Horizontal alignment: all main items are center-aligned. Beverage icons are distributed evenly along a single horizontal row with equal spacing and consistent icon tile size.
- Padding: page edge padding ~20–28px left/right. Vertical spacing between major sections ~18–28px.

States & interactions
- Tap a beverage "+" badge: triggers an animated micro-interaction: the icon slightly scales up (1.06x) while a small animated droplet moves from the icon to the mascot silhouette; the water fill level animates up smoothly to reflect added ounces. Easing: cubic-bezier(0.22, 0.8, 0.12, 1) (ease-out cubic) for the fill rise; duration ~600–900ms.
- Mascot fill animation: liquid surface waves gently (subtle periodic horizontal wave animation) and fill height animates per change in hydration percentage. Add a soft bounce when the fill reaches a milestone (25%, 50%, 100%).
- Day selector pill: acts as a segmented control; tapping toggles between days or opens a day picker. Pill transitions include slide of the circular day indicator and color fade.
- Top-right waves button: opens settings or quick filters (example: toggle drink types or view weekly trends) as a modal.
- Bottom tips card: draggable; tap expands to full-screen bottom sheet revealing tips list and interactions. Animation: slide up with 300–400ms ease-in-out.

Iconography & assets
- Beverage icons are flat, colorful illustrations with small details (tea bag string for green tea, coffee bean mark for coffee, straw for juice). Colors are saturated but within the palette (water: cyan, tea: green #7ED957, coffee: brown #6B3E2B, juice: orange #F4A300). Labels are muted uppercase gray.
- Small plus badges: white circular background with cyan plus symbol. They should be consistent size across icons (~20–26px diameter).

Accessibility notes
- Ensure contrast for the main numeric readout against white is compliant (use darker cyan if necessary). Provide alternative text for all icons and the mascot. Tap targets are 44–72px to meet touch target guidelines. Animate with reduced-motion preference respected.

Assets to recreate
- Large bear silhouette vector (single shape with inner mask for water). 
- A masked water surface vector that can be animated vertically.
- Five beverage icon vectors with matching color palette and small plus badge overlay assets.
- Rounded pink bottom sheet background and small decorative stickers on its right.

Misc
- Status bar mock (time 9:41) and iOS style carrier/wifi/battery indicators aligned top-right. The entire layout is clearly designed for a single vertically-scrolling mobile screen with an anchored bottom sheet and centered single-column structure.

Specific (single-screen) actions
- View current hydration amount: read the large numeric amount (e.g., “6.5oz”) at the top to quickly see intake for the day.
- See progress percentage: read the subtitle for percent of daily goal (e.g., "7% of your goal").
- Switch day / quick-select date: tap the top-left rounded pill (shows "1 day") to change tracked day or open a small day selector. The pill provides an immediate visual state for which day is shown.
- Open quick menu or filters: tap the circular top-right waves icon to open a modal/menu for filters, settings, or quick views (e.g., weekly history).
- Select a pet or avatar: tap the left-most avatar tile (Bear Bernard) to choose or personalize the mascot. The avatar tile includes a small control (possibly to edit name or costume).
- Log a drink: tap the "+" badge on any beverage icon in the horizontal row (Water, Green Tea, Coffee, Juice) to add a predefined quantity of that drink to the daily total. The UI gives immediate feedback via animation and updates the numeric readout and water fill.
- Inspect drink details: long-press or tap a drink icon for options (choose volume, edit amount, or remove entry).
- Expand tips / guidance: drag or tap the pink "Today's tips" bottom card to expand the bottom sheet and read multiple tips or tasks. The card also shows progress (e.g., "0/3") for tip completion, and individual tips can be tapped to mark done.
- Observe progress visually: watch the mascot illustration fill with water — a direct visual mapping of percentage progress.
- Access additional features when expanded: expanded bottom sheet likely shows more navigation, settings, or deeper metrics (history, achievements).

Medium-level workflows (combined actions)
- Quick logging workflow: user taps a drink icon +, sees a short animation of water traveling to the mascot, watches the numeric readout update, and sees the water fill rise — confirmation of successful logging. If desired, user adjusts the logged amount via a small modal triggered after tapping the +.
- Personalization flow: user taps the avatar tile to set or change the pet, opens a modal to pick a name or appearance, then returns to the home screen with the avatar updated.
- Daily routine / goal completion workflow: user checks the numeric value and % periodically, logs multiple drinks through the beverage row, and uses the tips card to complete suggested tasks to increase daily water — eventually reaching 100% which triggers celebratory animation on the mascot (e.g., confetti or sparkle).
- Learn & improve: user expands "Today's tips" to read educational content, taps links to learn why hydration matters, and then logs additional drinks.

Broader goal (purpose)
- The screen's overall purpose is to help users track and increase hydration in a friendly, gamified way. It combines numeric feedback (exact ounces and percent) with an emotional hook (a pet mascot that fills with water) to encourage consistent behavior. Visual clarity, immediate feedback, and easy logging reduce friction so users can quickly record drinks and see progress toward their daily water goal. The bottom tips card supports education and habit formation by surfacing small, actionable tips and showing progress toward completing them.

content.description:
Overview
- Full-screen, single-item product selection / add-to-order screen with a dominant central illustration of a green tea cup. Layout is minimal and highly centered with generous white space; most visual weight is on the cup illustration and one primary CTA.
Overall style
- Friendly, playful, minimal illustrative style. Flat, vector illustration with simple shapes and small decorative leaf motifs inside the cup. Visual language uses rounded corners and circular buttons, soft shadows and bold, highly legible typography.
Color palette (use these specific HEXs provided and a few functional neutrals)
- Primary green (cup, CTA background): #05C67E
- Secondary green (accent/alternate): #7EC605
- Deep text / dark accent: #352C23
- Background / canvas: #FBFBFB (near-white)
- Muted accent / translucent green: #9AC1B2
- Inactive/placeholder gray (used for unselected size text): #E6E6E6 (approx)
- Soft shadow color (subtle): rgba(53,44,35,0.06)
Typography
- System sans (recommend SF Pro Display / Inter / Roboto): large display and medium weights.
- Size examples (for 375pt wide iPhone baseline):
  - Main size label “12.0oz”: 36–40pt, weight 700 (bold), letter-spacing 0, color #352C23, center-aligned.
  - CTA label “+ GREEN TEA”: 18–20pt, weight 700 (bold/semibold), uppercase, letter-spacing 0.4–1.0pt, color white on green background.
  - Secondary size hint “16.0oz”: 18pt, weight 600, color very light gray (#E6E6E6), used to indicate neighboring carousel option.
UI components and states
- Illustration (cup)
  - Large vector occupying lower half of the screen. Cup shape is rounded rectangle with a flat handle to the right. Top rim has a thin light highlight (#FBFBFB or rgba white) to suggest surface.
  - Spoon / tea bag tab drawn in pale gray (#F0F2F3) hanging inside from the top rim.
  - Small leaf motifs inside cup in a lighter green (#9AC1B2) for texture.
  - A circular accent button overlay sits on the cup’s front (approx 56–64pt diameter) in a brighter green (#7EC605 or #05C67E depending on emphasis) with a small up/down chevron icon (dark #352C23). The accent has no heavy border but may include a tiny inner shadow to lift it.
- Top status / close control
  - Status bar at top (carrier/time/battery) left and right; top-right circular close button (white circular background with subtle drop shadow and an “X” icon in dark color) sized ~44pt with shadow: box-shadow: 0 10px 20px rgba(53,44,35,0.06).
- Size label
  - Big centered numeric label under illustration “12.0oz” (primary selected size). To the right and slightly faded is the next size “16.0oz” (muted, indicating a swipable carousel of sizes).
- Primary CTA
  - Large pill button centered near the bottom: green background #05C67E, text uppercase white + icon or leading plus sign. Height ~56–64pt, horizontal padding 36–40pt, border-radius 28–32pt. Bold type, visible touch target. Subtle inner shadow or top highlight to convey tactility.
- Secondary action / affordance
  - Small circular ghost button to the right of CTA (pale green circular with 6-dot grid icon) used to reveal options/menu. Diameter ~44pt, background #F4FFF2 or #EAF9EE, icon in #7EC605.
- Micro-interactions and animations (recommended)
  - Cup illustration: gentle pop/scale on load (scale 0.98 -> 1.0), 220ms, easing cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1).
  - Accent circle (chevrons): on tap, animate chevrons to indicate toggle state (chevron rotate or move), 120ms.
  - Size selector: horizontal swipe/drag to switch sizes with a carousel motion and fading of the next size label; each page snap ~320ms, easing cubic-bezier(.22,.9,.3,1).
  - CTA press: brief scale down 0.96 then rebound (120ms) with subtle shadow change.
Layout specifics (dimensions and spacing suggestions for 375pt width)
- Safe/top area: 44pt (status area). Close button is positioned in top-right within safe area with 16pt margin from edges.
- Illustration container: starts about 140–160pt from top (below status) and extends down to ~420–460pt from top — roughly 45–55% of screen height.
- Main size label placed 16–24pt below illustration baseline.
- CTA area: CTA centered horizontally; bottom edge sits ~44–64pt above bottom safe area. Vertical spacing between size label and CTA ~24–32pt.
- Padding: horizontal padding for content ~24–28pt.
Accessibility
- Use high-contrast copy for primary text (#352C23 on near-white background). Provide accessible contrast for CTA text (white on #05C67E ~4.5:1 maybe; check and darken CTA if needed).
Assets & icons
- Use vector SVGs for cup and small icons. Chevron icons within circular accent should be simple 2–3px stroke, rounded caps.
Notes to developer / designer
- Visual emphasis must be on single product selection — use big illustration, bold size label and a prominent single CTA.
- Keep composition vertically stacked in a single centered column. Avoid extra chrome or dense controls.
- For different sizes, a swipeable carousel or horizontal pagination is appropriate; show neighboring size values faded to hint at more options.
- Use the provided main greens for brand identity; use the darker #352C23 for content and icons.
content.layout:
Overall structure
- Single-column, vertically stacked layout (1 main column). All primary elements are centered along the vertical axis.
- Main vertical groups (top to bottom):
  1) Status/close area (top safe area)
  2) Illustration area (large cup graphic with overlay controls)
  3) Size label / carousel hint (centered numeric label, with next size partially visible to right)
  4) CTA & small action button area (primary pill CTA centered, small circular options button to the right)
- Columns and groups: there is effectively 1 column for primary content; within the CTA group there is a visual two-item row: large pill CTA (centered) and a small circular secondary action aligned to the right of it. This can be treated as a 2-column micro-group inside the single-column layout.
- Grid: not a rigid grid; the screen follows a stacked flow with consistent vertical rhythm (top area / hero / label / CTA). If you implement a grid it’s a single-column 12pt baseline grid with major vertical spacings of 16–32pt.
- Alignment and padding: central alignment; horizontal padding ~24pt from edges for any text-based content. Illustration intentionally bleeds visually to the sides but maintains safe-zone spacing so that the handle and cup are not clipped by device edges.

- centered
- stacked-vertical
- hero-illustration
- spacious
- bottom-CTA
- modal-like
- carousel-hint
- floating-actions
- rounded-pill-buttons
content.functions:
Specific actions (what users can do on this screen)
- Dismiss/close: tap the top-right circular X button to close this full-screen modal or overlay (instant close animation, 160ms).
- Inspect product: view the large cup illustration and read the selected size label (12.0oz). The illustration is primarily decorative but reinforces product selection.
- Change size: swipe horizontally on the size label or the illustration to navigate between available sizes (e.g., 12.0oz, 16.0oz). The next size appears to the right in muted text indicating unselected state. Also possible: tap left/right chevrons (if present) or the circular chevron accent on the cup.
- Toggle detail/option: tap the circular overlay on the cup (green circle with chevrons) to reveal additional info or to toggle a simple state (e.g., temperature or strength). This control gives contextual interaction tied to the product image.
- Add to order: tap the primary CTA pill "+ GREEN TEA" to add the selected drink (with chosen size) to the cart or start the next step in a flow. Provide immediate feedback (toast or animated microinteraction) confirming addition.
- Open more options: tap the small pale circular button (6-dot grid) to open secondary options or an actions sheet (e.g., customize, view nutrition, pick add-ons).
- Implicit gestures: vertical drag down or swipe/close gesture may also dismiss this overlay.
Medium-level workflows
- Select size → optionally toggle option (chevrons) → tap + GREEN TEA to add item → receive confirmation and return to previous screen or continue to cart.
- Explore options → tap small options button → present bottom sheet with add-ons (milk, sweetener, etc.) → confirm.
Broader purpose
- The screen’s primary goal is to let a user choose a specific beverage (green tea) and size, then add it to their order quickly. The design emphasizes speed and delight: clear selection (size), an inviting CTA, and a strong visual to reduce friction when making the purchase/selection decision.

content.description:
Overall style
- Clean, playful onboarding/dashboard screen with large central illustration and bright, kid-friendly colors. Visual language mixes flat illustration with soft shadows and round shapes; the tone is friendly and light.
- Primary typeface: rounded humanist system type (recommend SF Pro Display / Avenir Next / Nunito). Use generous tracking and large sizes for the main metric. Secondary text uses a medium weight and muted gray. Labels use uppercase small caps with letter spacing.

Color palette (use provided main colors and helpers)
- Cyan / Accent: #34BBEC (used for primary metric, plus buttons, water fill)
- Green / Fill: #04C47C (used for part-fill of illustration legs, callout elements)
- Mustard / Accent: #D3BD11 (accent sparingly for badges or small UI accents)
- Deep Violet: #41386F (supporting color for heavy text or dark icons if needed)
- Light Blue Gray: #9EBBD2 (muted secondary UI backgrounds, soft icons)
- Body background: #FFFFFF (full-screen white)
- Silhouette / very light: #F0F2F4 (large giraffe silhouette)
- Muted copy: #9AA0A6 (subtitle and lower-case labels)

Typography
- Heading / metric ("15.5oz"): SF Pro Display Bold or 800 weight; size ~56–72px (about 48–60pt) depending on density; color #34BBEC; centered; line-height ~1.0–1.1; tracking neutral.
- Subtitle ("Hydration · 17% of your goal"): SF Pro Text Medium 16–18px; color #9AA0A6; centered; small icon (water droplet) at end sized ~18px.
- Item labels (WATER, GREEN TEA, COFFEE): Uppercase, SF Pro Text Semibold 12–13px; color #B6BDC3 (very muted grey); letter-spacing +1.2px; centered below each icon.
- Onboarding CTA ("Finish your setup"): Rounded button text, SF Pro Text SemiBold 18–20px; color #FF3B6D or bright pink for CTA text (in screenshot it’s pink); placed inside a soft rounded bottom sheet.

Layout and spacing
- Screen is a single-column vertical layout, center-aligned.
- Status bar area: native iOS status icons at very top; leave ~12–16px top safe area.
- Top controls: two circular control icons horizontally aligned beyond the center line: top-left circular turquoise badge (diameter ~48px) with small numeric label (white). Top-right circular white pill (diameter ~44px) with three wavy lines icon (dark gray). Both have subtle drop shadows (rgba(65,56,111,0.06), 0 6px 16px).
- Main metric block: placed under the status area and centered. Vertical spacing: ~28–36px under top icons.
  - Big numeric label (15.5oz) centered, large cyan #34BBEC. Beneath it a single-line subtitle: muted gray text and a small droplet icon left or right.
- Illustration area: large giraffe silhouette centered below metric, occupying majority of vertical space. The silhouette is light gray (#F0F2F4) with a soft inner shadow. Legs are partially filled with two colors to indicate progress: lower segment filled with cyan #34BBEC for the immediate liquid and the mid segment filled with green #04C47C above it. The fills are aligned to the bottom of the leg shapes and have a crisp top edge (no gradient). Each leg fill width matches the leg silhouette edges; fill height corresponds to hydration percent.
- Bottom drink selector: horizontally centered row of 5 tappable drink items (icons) near the lower third of screen. Each icon sits inside a circular/rounded container or is a flat illustrated glyph above a small uppercase label. Spacing: equal horizontal gaps; each tile ~64–80px wide; icons sized ~44px–56px. Each icon has a small circular plus overlay near the bottom center of the icon (diameter ~22px) with background #34BBEC and white plus glyph.
  - From left to right: avatar/giraffe profile chip (circular illustrated avatar with subtle background), Water (tall glass icon), Green Tea (cup with leaf icon, green #04C47C), Coffee (brown cup with coffee bean), Juice (orange cup with straw). Labels beneath each icon in muted gray.
- Bottom sheet / banner: a rounded capsule panel anchored to the bottom with a pale sky-blue background (#EAF7FB or use #DFF6FB) containing a step indicator bubble ("2/3" in a pink oval) left, and a pink CTA text "Finish your setup" centered. A small character illustration peeks out from the right edge of the bottom sheet. Panel height ~84–110px, with 12–16px inner padding and corner radius ~28–36px.

UI components and states
- Tappable drink tiles: default state: flat illustrated icon with plus badge. On tap: animate small bounce, plus -> check, liquid fills increase on giraffe legs and the main metric updates numerically with a short morphing animation. Use 200–350ms animation with ease-out cubic bezier (cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)). Provide micro-feedback: ripple or scale to 0.98 while pressed.
- Leg fill animation: animated vertical fill growing from bottom to target height over 450ms with ease-out; fill colors remain solid cyan/green; add subtle horizontal wave at top (very faint) to suggest liquid movement (use small 6–8px wave amplitude, 1–2s loop if persistent). Low CPU cost: simple mask reveal or height animation.
- Top-left round progress badge: numeric step — on tap it might open a profile or show progress details. Subtle shadow and small outer arc indicating completion.
- Top-right menu (three wavy lines): toggles a concise menu, slide-in or popover.
- Bottom CTA: tapping "Finish your setup" proceeds to next onboarding step or completes account setup.

Iconography & illustrations
- All icons are flat, slightly rounded, with subtle highlights. Use an illustrated mascot (giraffe) for avatar and large silhouette for hero.
- Plus badges: small circular turquoise #34BBEC with white plus; drop shadow minimal.

Spacing & grid
- The vertical rhythm uses ~8px baseline increments. Horizontal content is center aligned; containment max width 420px for large phones.
- Drink selector is a single horizontal group (1 row, 5 columns) centered with equal spacing. The overall layout is essentially a single column with three major vertical groups: header (controls + metric), hero (illustration & dynamic fills), footer (drinks + bottom sheet).

Accessibility
- Ensure contrast for important text: big metric uses large size to be readable; provide descriptive labels for icons; hit area for tappable icons >=44x44px.

Assets to replicate
- Giraffe silhouette vector (light gray), four leg mask shapes to animate fills independently.
- Drink glyphs as vector icons with small overlay plus buttons.
- Rounded bottom sheet background with progress pill and CTA text.

Animation summary
- Metric number: crossfade / count-up animation 300–450ms ease-out.
- Leg fills: height reveal animation 400–600ms ease-out; optional subtle wave animation on fill top 1–2s loop with low opacity.
- Icon tap: quick scale 85–120ms press, then bounce back 220ms.

Notes for developers/designers
- Use SVG for vector illustrations and mask legs for efficient fill animations.
- Keep entire layout responsive: on narrow screens reduce metric font-size and scale down giraffe to keep drink selector and bottom sheet visible.
content.layout:
Overall structure
- Single-column center-aligned layout with three vertical regions:
  1) Header region: status bar + two small circular controls (top-left numeric turquoise badge, top-right white menu button) and the large metric block beneath centered.
  2) Main region: large centered illustrated giraffe silhouette occupying the vertical middle, with leg shapes masked to allow independent fills (cyan and green fill segments). This region has the most visual weight.
  3) Footer region: horizontal selection row of drink icons (one row, five columns), and a rounded bottom sheet anchored to bottom with onboarding CTA and step indicator.

Columns & groups
- The layout effectively uses 1 primary column for main content (metric + illustration). Within the footer group there is a horizontal five-column group for drink selectors (1 row, 5 equal columns). The bottom sheet sits full-width but visually as an overlay panel with large radius.

Grid & spacing
- Use an 8px baseline grid. The drink icons are placed in a single row grid with equal spacing; each column width approx 20% of the screen minus gutters. The hero region is centered with fluid height; the giraffe vector scales to keep the drink row visible above the bottom sheet.

Keywords to describe layout
- center-aligned
- single-column
- hero-illustration
- horizontal selector row
- masked-fill regions
- bottom-sheet CTA
- top controls
- large numeric metric
- generous white space
- equal-width icon columns
content.functions:
Small / Specific actions
- Tap a drink icon (WATER, GREEN TEA, COFFEE, JUICE): adds that drink to the user’s hydration total. Visual feedback: icon plus badge animates (press scale) and the giraffe’s leg fills grow to reflect added fluid; the central metric (e.g., "15.5oz") updates to the new total with a short count-up animation.
- Tap the profile avatar (GIRAFFE GIOVANNI): opens profile or personalization sheet for the mascot (change avatar or view details).
- Tap the top-left numeric badge: view step or progress explanation; could open an onboarding step list. Tap the top-right wavy-lines icon: open auxiliary menu or settings.
- Tap the plus badge on any drink: a direct, single-action increment. Long-press on a drink could open a quantity picker (optional).
- Tap the bottom CTA ("Finish your setup"): completes the current onboarding task and advances to the next flow.

Medium-level workflows
- Add multiple drinks: users repeatedly tap icons; each tap increments ounces and immediately updates both the numeric display and the giraffe leg fills. The UI maintains a consistent visual mapping (fluid volume <-> leg fill height) so users can understand impact at a glance.
- Personalize character: from the avatar tile the user can change the mascot. This links the onboarding personalization with the hydration tracking dashboard.
- Reveal breakdown: tapping the main metric or a small info icon next to the subtitle could expand a summary list (time-stamped entries), offering a history of drinks added.

Broader goals
- Primary goal: onboard the user to the hydration-tracking feature and get the user to add their first drinks — conveyed via an inviting illustration, large progress metric, and easily tappable drink icons.
- Secondary goals: personalize the experience (giraffe avatar), demonstrate cause-and-effect (tap drink -> legs fill -> metric increases), and lead the user to complete setup (Finish your setup CTA in bottom sheet). The design prioritizes clarity and fast wins (users feel accomplished after first taps), and uses gamified visuals (mascot fills) to encourage continued interaction.

How UI supports goals
- Large metric and progress percent provide immediate feedback and motivation.
- The visual mapping (liquid fills on giraffe) provides an intuitive progress metaphor that’s memorable for kids and adults alike.
- Bottom drink icons are large, recognizable, and have direct action affordances (plus badges) to reduce friction for adding drinks.
- Step indicator and "Finish your setup" CTA make onboarding status obvious and guide the user through completion.

records.name: Hydration Summary
records.description: Summary (happy path): The user opens the Hydration Summary screen in portrait mobile. The top circular metric shows a headline stat (percentage or streak). A segmented control directly below switches aggregation between Days / Weeks / Months. The main card displays a stacked-bar visualization with labels (oz) and a color-coded legend that breaks down drink types and their percentages. A monthly calendar grid is shown beneath the card. Entry point: user navigates to the hydration/tracking area of the product. Exit points: user taps the close (X) button or navigates away using app chrome (not shown). Assumptions: user is signed in and has recorded drinks for the displayed time ranges; device is a mobile phone in portrait orientation.
records.problem: User task: Quickly inspect hydration progress and the composition of drinks over selectable time ranges (days or weeks) and locate calendar dates with entries. From the user's perspective they want to: (1) see a headline metric (today's hydration percentage or streak), (2) view an aggregated stacked-bar chart for recent days or weekly averages, (3) identify how much each drink type contributed via the legend, and (4) reference the calendar for specific dates. From the interface perspective the UI provides: a prominent circular KPI, a segmented control for selecting aggregation (Days / Weeks / Months), a stacked bar visualization with per-column labels and color-coded segments, a legend showing percent share by drink type, and a monthly calendar underneath. Result: User-perceived outcome — the user understands their current hydration status (percentage or streak), recent consumption volumes (oz) and drink composition, and can find relevant dates on the calendar. System-level outcome — the UI renders the selected aggregation of recorded drink data into the circular KPI, stacked bars, and legend; the calendar reflects recorded-day indicators; the segmented control updates the chart and KPI when toggled.

content.description:
Mobile hydration-tracking dashboard, single-column vertical layout optimized for a phone (approx. 375pt wide). Top area: system status indicators (time at left, signal/wifi/battery at right) on a white/near-white background. Below this, centered circular progress badge (diameter ~140–170px) with a solid cyan/turquoise fill (#0ABEC1) showing large percentage ("22%") in white, bold, sans-serif (approx. 48–56pt) and two-line supporting label beneath ("TODAY'S / HYDRATION") in uppercase, tighter tracking, ~12–14pt. The circle has a short sculpted arc accent at top-right that uses a slightly darker cyan gradient for depth. A small circular close button (white circle with subtle drop shadow and dark × icon) floats near the top-right corner of the screen area.

Main card: a large rounded-rectangle card (full width minus 32–40px horizontal margin, radius ~20–28px) sits below the progress badge on a very light grey background (#FBFBFB). Card background is slightly off-white (#F6F7F8) with a faint inner shadow and generous vertical padding (~24–28px). At the top-left of the card is a segmented control / tabs row with three segments: "Days" (active, filled with white and small shadow), "Weeks" and "Months" (inactive, muted grey). Segmented control pill has subtle border and about 40–44px height; labels use the same rounded sans font at ~14–16pt. On the right of the segmented control there is a small colorful circular icon (illustration of a cup / drink) used as visual branding.

Below the tabs is a centered title "Last 7 days" (dark navy text #372F77, ~20–24pt, medium weight). The chart region occupies the middle of the card: a 7-column stacked-bar visualization. Each column represents a day of the week (columns count = 7). Columns are built from stacked rounded "pills" (rounded rectangles with large corner radius, height ~14–22px, width ~44–52px) each pill colored by drink type (examples: Water - cyan #0ABEC1; Milk - pale grey #E9EEF0; Green Tea - light green ~#C6F27A; Coffee - brown ~#8A4B3F; Beer - warm yellow ~#F2D16B; Juice/red drinks - #B4293B; additional accent colors for variety). Each column shows a small cyan label above the stack with total oz value (e.g., "90oz", "92oz") in bold ~12pt cyan text. X-axis weekday initials sit under the chart in a muted grey; active/selected day letters are cyan. The stacks have consistent horizontal spacing; columns vary in total height to reflect daily totals.

Under the chart is a thin horizontal divider (light grey line). Beneath that is a legend represented as rounded chips (Tags & Chips) showing percent share and drink name. Each chip has a light colored oval background matching the drink color and a small bold percentage (e.g., "22%") and label (e.g., "Water") next to it. Chips have spacing between them and use small type ~12–13pt. The card's inner padding and spacing are generous to create an airy feel.

Below the card, the calendar/month header is rendered: a large month title centered ("April") in dark navy #372F77, large weight and ~36–44pt size. Under it is a lightweight calendar row of weekday initials (S M T W T F S) in cyan for active or selectable ones, and a dotted grid of circular day indicators (light grey circles) forming the calendar body; these small circles look like page controls / date placeholders. Overall composition uses a lot of white space and subtle shadows to create depth.

Color palette (primary & notable colors):
- Cyan / Teal (primary accent): #0ABEC1 (main progress circle & water labels)
- Yellow (accent): #DCBD0A (secondary accent for beer/chips)
- Dark navy: #372F77 (typography headings)
- Off-white / page background: #FBFBFB
- Red: #B4293B (accent for some drink stacks or badges)
- Additional suggested colors for legend stacks: Milk/pale grey #E9EEF0, Green Tea #CFF07D, Coffee Brown #8A4B3F, Beer #F2D16B

Typography: clean rounded sans-serif (system iOS "SF Pro" / "SF Pro Display" or similar). Suggested scale: month heading 36–44pt bold; card title 20–24pt semibold; segmented control labels and legend labels 12–16pt medium; large percentage in circular badge 48–56pt heavy; oz labels above stacks 10–12pt bold in cyan; line-height kept tight for labels (1.0–1.2). All text left/center aligned consistently as shown (titles centered; tab labels left-aligned within pill).

Spacing & sizing (approximate for 375pt width): left/right outer margin 16pt; card horizontal padding 18–20pt; vertical spacing between progress circle and card ~20–28pt; chart area height ~220–260px; pill stack width ~44–52pt; pill height ~14–20pt; gap between columns ~20–26pt. Rounded radii: large ~28px for card corners; pill radius equal to half pill height for capsule look; segmented control radius ~22px.

UI states & micro-interactions: the circular progress animates from 0→22% on load with a smooth ease-out (duration ~600ms) and small overshoot; the stacked bars animate upward from base (duration ~600–800ms, staggered per column). Tabs change background / foreground state with a 200ms fade and a slight slide of the white fill. Tapping any bar or pill shows a subtle tooltip or ephemeral overlay with exact measurement and time; legend chips are tappable to toggle visibility of that drink type in the chart (faded state for hidden items). The close button has a 44px tappable diameter and a subtle shadow to indicate elevation.
content.layout:
Single-column mobile layout with three vertical groups stacked top-to-bottom:
1) Header group (system status + floating close button + large circular progress center) — single full-width column centered horizontally.
2) Main card group — a full-width rounded card containing a segmented control (single row), a centered title, a 7-column stacked-bar chart (grid-like structure inside the card), a horizontal divider, and a legend (chips) row. The card content is vertically stacked inside one main column but the chart itself uses a 7-column sub-grid representing days; each column is a vertical stack (variable height) of rounded pills.
   - Chart sub-grid: columns = 7 (one per day). Rows are not uniform — number of stack items varies, but visually each pill defines a row; overall chart height is constant.
3) Calendar & month group — a centered large month title, a weekday initials row (7 columns), and a grid of circular day indicators (approx. 5 rows x 7 columns) shown as dotted placeholders.

Column & grouping counts: primary layout contains 1 main column; the key internal grid is the chart with 7 columns. Legend chips are laid out in a horizontal flow (wrap if needed). The segmented control contains 3 segments (Days, Weeks, Months) acting visually as three columns inside the control.

Key layout details: generous vertical white space between groups, large centered headings, consistent horizontal margins (approx. 16pt), rounded card corners (20–28px), and pill-shaped stack elements creating a soft, friendly visual rhythm. Visual hierarchy is created with scale (large percentage > card title > chip labels) and color contrast (bright cyan for primary actions and labels, deep navy for headings).
content.functions:
Specific user actions on this screen:
- Tap the circular close button (top-right) to dismiss the view.
- Read today's hydration percentage in the central progress badge (informational-only).
- Tap the segmented control (Days / Weeks / Months) to switch time granularity; the chart animates to reflect the selected range.
- Tap an individual bar column (any day) to reveal details for that day (a tooltip or modal with exact breakdown and timestamps).
- Tap a legend chip (percentage + drink name) to toggle that drink type on/off in the stacked chart; the chart reflows and updates totals.
- Scroll vertically to reach the calendar view below and select a specific date by tapping a day indicator.
- Use the month header to navigate months (tap to open full month selector or swipe to move months) — or tap specific week/day letters.

Medium-level workflows enabled by the UI:
- Inspect short-term trends: switching "Days/Weeks/Months" lets users compare hydration at different granularities; stacked bars show composition by drink type for each interval.
- Diagnose beverage contributions: legend chips and color-coded stacks let users identify which drinks contribute most to hydration over the selected period (tap to isolate water vs. other drinks).
- Drill down from overview to detail: select a single day from the stack or calendar to view a timeline or list of drink entries for that day (not shown but implied via interactions).
- Month navigation: the month header and calendar dots let users move through historical data quickly.

Broader goals the user achieves:
- Monitor daily and weekly hydration relative to a target, quickly seeing percent complete and trends.
- Understand the composition of fluid intake (water vs. milk, coffee, beer, etc.) enabling behavioral changes (e.g., increase water, reduce soda).
- Track progress over time and identify days/weeks with low intake so the user can adjust routines or set reminders. The interface emphasizes clarity and low friction: big numerical feedback, clear color-coded breakdowns, and simple controls to change range and filter categories.

records.name: Share celebration poster

Entry point: daily goal completion / celebration screen. Exit point: external social composer with the poster inserted. Assumptions: user is signed in (or not required) and has network access; the device has the target social app installed and allows cross-app paste/sharing; the app has permission to present an in-app share sheet and invoke system or third-party share targets.
records.problem: User task: from the user's perspective they want to celebrate and share that they reached a daily hydration goal by creating a polished image and posting it to social channels. They expect an attractive, ready-to-share graphic, a simple way to choose where to share, and the chosen social composer to open with the image already inserted. Interface/system perspective: the UI provides a celebratory landing screen with a clear CTA to create a shareable asset; a poster generator that composes branding, mascot art, day label, and stats; a share sheet listing messaging and social targets; and integration to paste or hand off the generated image into third-party composers. End result: user-perceived outcome — a visually pleasing poster is created and opened in the selected social composer ready to post. content.description:
Overall style: Bright, playful mobile celebration/achievement screen with a large centered illustrated mascot, confetti animation and strong rounded shapes. Primary palette (from provided colors): turquoise/cyan #1DB9E8, bright green #14BE7E, olive #899237, yellow #E0BF0D, dark brown #3B3127. Supporting neutrals: pure white background #FFFFFF and muted gray text #9B9B9B for secondary copy. Accent dark CTA color: very dark navy/charcoal #1B2630 (used for primary pill CTA background).

Background: Solid white full-bleed background (#FFFFFF). Sparse confetti scattered over the entire screen — small rectangles in cyan (#1DB9E8), green (#14BE7E), purple (approx #9B7BE0), orange/yellow (#E0BF0D) and pink (#FF7FA3). Confetti sits in front of and behind hero illustration to give depth.

Top area / status: Topmost area respects device status bar (time left-aligned and status icons right-aligned). Top-left there is a circular user avatar badge (40–48px diameter) with a teal outline ring (approx 4px) and a brown filled center (#3B3127) containing a white check icon. Top-right is a circular white action button (44px) with a subtle shadow and an icon of three wavy lines (menu/filter) in dark gray (#4A4A4A).

Heading & subtitle: Centered below the top area is a large headline “Cheerful Tuesday!” rendered in a rounded grotesque/sans (think Nunito/Quicksand/Poppins with heavy roundness). Size ≈ 44–56pt on iPhone-scale, weight semibold to bold (600–700). Color: bright turquoise (#1DB9E8). Letterspacing normal (0 to +1px); centered alignment. Subtitle directly under headline is a single line of smaller secondary text “91.6oz hydration • 101% of your goal” with a small droplet icon on the right. Subtitle font size ≈ 14–16pt, weight regular (400), color medium gray #9B9B9B.

Hero illustration: Large centered mascot silhouette (chameleon/monkey hybrid perched on a branch) occupying the vertical middle of the screen. The illustration is made of stacked horizontal color bands (green #14BE7E, cyan #1DB9E8, olive #899237, brown #3B3127, light gray fill for some sections). Size: approximately 55–65% of screen height; perfectly centered horizontally. The illustration is flat, vector-style, slightly desaturated mid-tones with smooth rounded edges. It intentionally has a cut-out look with colored stripes.

Confetti & animation: Confetti pieces overlay the entire screen, animated to fall slowly from top to bottom, rotating and fading out near the bottom. Confetti colors match the palette. Subtle particle motion: 3–6s duration, randomized delays, ease-out cubic, slight horizontal drift.

Primary CTA (“Celebrate my day!”): A rounded pill-shaped callout sits near the lower-mid area overlapping the bottom of the hero illustration. Pill dimensions ≈ 260px width × 56px height on 375pt width baseline, corner radius ≈ 28px. Background: dark charcoal/navy (#1B2630) with white bold text (16–18pt, 600). To the left of the label is a small square thumbnail (48px) with a 4px pale-blue border (soft drop-shadow) showing a miniature of the hero illustration. The pill casts a subtle elevation shadow (rgba(27,38,48,0.12), blur 12px, offset-y 6px).

Drink quick-add row: Near the bottom above the cream streak card is a horizontal row of five drink icons evenly spaced with labels beneath. Each drink item is vertically arranged: a circular/rounded icon (approx 56×56px) with a small circular plus badge (18–22px) overlaid near the bottom center (or bottom-right) of each icon. The five illustrated icons: Capuchin avatar (profile/character), Water (tall blue cup), Pumpkin Latte (tall glass with whipped top), Green Tea (green mug with tea bag), Milk (bottle gray). Each icon uses a simplified flat illustration style and the primary palette. Beneath each icon is a small label in uppercase small-caps light gray (10–12pt) — examples: CAPUCHIN, WATER, PUMPKIN LATTE, GREEN TEA, MILK. Spacing between items ≈ 18–24px. Tapping any plus adds that drink to the log.

Bottom card / streak: At the very bottom there is a rounded cream/beige card that spans nearly full width with large radius (approx 18–22px). Inside is a coffee/streak related line “Escape Caffeine Capuchin ✓ 9d” with a coffee bean icon on the left. Text is medium brown (#3B3127) semi-bold (600) at 16–18pt. The beige card slightly overlaps the bottom safe area and has a soft shadow.

Typography: Primary heading uses a rounded geometric sans (large size, semibold). Secondary/subhead and labels use a neutral sans (regular weight). Small caps or uppercase labels for the drink names. Leading: heading line-height ~1.05–1.15, subtitle line-height ~1.4.

Spacing & layout grid: Single-column centered layout. Side gutters ≈ 24–28pt on mobile. Vertical rhythm: status bar to headline ~28–36pt, headline to subtitle 8–12pt, subtitle to hero 22–32pt, hero to CTA pill ~18–28pt, CTA to drink icons ~18–24pt, drink icons to bottom card ~12–18pt.

States and micro-interactions:
- Drink icons: tap states show a small ripple or scale-down (0.96) and then a '+1' micro-toast + hydration number increment animation; plus badge pulses for 300ms.
- CTA pill: on tap shows a share sheet or confetti burst (shorter, 1s) with a raised scale animation (1.05) and returns to rest.

Accessibility: Large readable heading, >4.5:1 contrast on CTA text vs dark pill, large tappable hit areas (min 44×44pt), labels provided for icons, and color not used as sole status indicator.

Recreation notes: Use vector shapes for the mascot with flat fills and crisp edges. Apply layered SVG confetti elements with randomized animation durations using CSS or Lottie for smoother performance. Use shadows sparingly and keep the main background clean white.

content.description:
General overview
- Portrait, single-screen splash/dashboard with a large bold typographic header at the top, a short rounded-corner message bubble below it (with a small circular avatar overlapping the left of the bubble), a large centered illustrated mascot silhouette (striped horizontally with brand colors) taking the middle of the screen, and a compact metrics row near the bottom with 5–6 small drink icons, a large numeric "oz" metric, and a short footer brand line.
Viewport & spacing
- Designed for a tall phone viewport (approx. 375px wide base). Safe-area top inset ~44px. Page horizontal padding 24–32px; main vertical spacing between major groups ~24–48px.
Background
- Solid white background: #FFFFFF.
Color palette (primary colors from screenshot)
- Cyan / Bright Aqua: #15BDE1 (main headline, border, some stripes, metric color)
- Bright Green: #10BA7E (stripe color and small icons)
- Dark Navy / Charcoal: #373A50 (primary body / footer text)
- Olive / Mustard hint: #898E3A (accent, may appear in small elements)
- Warm Yellow (accent): #E0BF08 (accent color present in palette sample)
- Neutral light gray for mascot stripe: #D6D9DD (approx.)
- Brown for cup/icon base: #6B3A2A (approx.)
Typography
- Headline: friendly rounded geometric sans with heavy weight. Suggested fonts: Baloo 2, Fredoka One or Poppins ExtraBold with rounded adjustments.
  - Two-line headline: first line small-caps/combination "MYcheerful" and second line large "TUESDAY".
  - Sizes (for 375px base): first line ~48–64px, second line ~72–96px. Weight: 700–900. Line-height tight (0.95–1.05) to visually overlap as seen.
  - Color: #15BDE1 for both lines.
- Message bubble text: rounded sans (e.g., Nunito Sans / Poppins SemiBold)
  - Font-size ~16–18px, weight 600, line-height 1.25, color #15BDE1 (same cyan) or slightly darker for readability.
- Footer / body text: dark navy #373A50
  - Body size ~14px–16px, weight 600 for brand name and 600 for CTA phrase in cyan. The link/CTA portion uses the cyan to stand out.
UI components & styling details
- Headline treatment: uppercase/combination with large tracking slightly reduced on second line. Letters have very rounded terminals.
- Message bubble: rounded rectangle with 3–4px cyan (#15BDE1) stroke, 12–16px vertical padding and 18–22px horizontal padding, maximum width ~78% of viewport, centered horizontally. Border radius ~26–30px. The bubble background is transparent (white) — only stroke is visible.
- Avatar: small circular mascot face sits overlapping left edge of the message bubble by ~10–12px. Diameter ~40px. Has a subtle drop shadow or none; sits vertically centered to bubble.
- Mascot silhouette (hero illustration): centered, large, occupying about 55–65% of screen height and ~70% of screen width. The shape is a single flat silhouette layered with horizontal color bands (stripes). Stripes are crisp, without gradients, with 5–6 different colors (cyan, dark navy, green, neutral gray, brown). Edges are clean vector shapes; silhouette has subtle playful details (tail curl, perched on a branch) but is flat colored.
  - Stripe proportions: top stripe (cyan head) ~14% of the silhouette height; next stripe (dark navy torso) ~18%; middle stripe (green) ~12%; next stripe (light gray) ~22%; lower-striped tail segments alternating cyan, green, and brown; each stripe has 0–2px separation (no stroke).
- Bottom icon row: a horizontal row of small drink icons (coffee cup, mug, bottle, milkshake, glass, etc.). Each icon is 28–42px square, evenly spaced horizontally (~16–24px gap), centered. Icons use flat fills with the palette (green, brown, gray, cyan). They are simple glyph-style illustrations without labels.
- Metric block: to the right of icon row or integrated with it, a vertical metric showing "oz" in small caps and the numeric value "91" in large cyan text. "oz" use small 18–20px weight 700; number uses ~44–56px bold cyan (#15BDE1).
- Footer line: centered under icons — left part "Waterllama.com" in dark navy #373A50 bold, right part "Stay hydrated & happy!" in cyan #15BDE1 bold. Font-size ~14–16px.
Borders, shapes & micro-detail
- Rounded corners dominate (avatar, bubble, letters, icons). No heavy drop shadows — design is flat and playful, minimal depth.
- All illustration edges are crisp vector shapes; no photographic textures.
- No visible interactive controls (no buttons, switches) on this screen; it's primarily informative/encouraging.
Animation notes (if any)
- If animated, recommended micro-animations: subtle breathing/pulse of the cyan headline (scale 1.0 → 1.02 over 1.6s ease-in-out, loop), a gentle float/bob on the mascot silhouette (translateY ±6–10px, 3s ease-in-out), and small bounce when a new drink is added to the metric (number briefly scales 1.0 → 1.12 over 220ms ease-out). Speech bubble can slide in from left on entrance (transform X -24px → 0, 300ms ease-out).
Accessibility
- Ensure headline color on white has sufficient contrast; if not, darken cyan slightly for AA. Provide alt text for mascot and icons. Ensure text sizes are scalable.
Assets to export / layers to create
- Headline as vector text with outlined copy available.
- Speech bubble as rounded rect stroke with separate avatar circle.
- Mascot silhouette as layered vector with separate stripe shapes exported as SVG.
- Individual drink icons as separate SVGs (30–48px artboard).
- Metric digits as vector or export as text layer styled with font for localization.
Implementation hints
- Use a single centered column layout with stacked blocks. Keep mobile-first spacing. Use SVG for mascot to keep crisp stripes and to animate if desired.

content.description:
Overall visual: A full-screen Instagram Story composition with a white background and a large, colorful mascot illustration (chameleon/llama-like creature) centered vertically. Top area: Large stacked headline reading “MYcheerful TUESDAY” in an all-caps rounded geometric sans (heavy weight). The headline color is bright turquoise/teal. Below the headline is a rounded speech-bubble style info box with a thin turquoise stroke and white fill (or very pale tint). Inside the bubble is a short congratulatory message in medium-weight sans serif: “Woohoo! You did it! Aim for a glass before every meal to stay hydrated. Stay hydrated” with a small circular emoji/avatar on the left of the bubble.

Center hero: A single large silhouette / illustration of a sitting chameleon/mascot on a branch. The mascot is made of horizontal color bands (stripes) — alternating turquoise/teal, lime green, light gray, and a brown tail tip — giving a layered flat-vector look. The illustration is vertically centered, occupying ~45–55% of the screen height. The mascot is flat, with no drop shadow; internal stripes have sharp edges and consistent stroke widths.

Bottom area: A horizontal row of small drink icons (cup, mug, travel cup, milk bottle, smoothie, full glass) spaced evenly above the bottom controls. To the right of the icons is a prominent hydration counter “oz 91” — the number large and bold in the same turquoise/teal as the headline; the “oz” label is smaller, stacked or aligned to the top-right of the number. Under the icon row is a short brand line: “Waterllama.com Stay hydrated & happy!” where the domain is bold dark gray and the tagline is turquoise/teal.

Native Instagram overlays (dark rounded elements on top of the content): Top-left has an X (close) inside a dark gray circular button. Center-top is a rounded white pill notification with faint shadow that reads “Instagram pasted from Waterllama.” Top-right a vertical stack of circular gray buttons (approx five) aligned along the right edge. Each circular button contains a white icon: “Aa” (text), smiley (stickers), music note, sparkles/filters, and a down caret. They are evenly spaced with ~12–18 px between them.

Bottom native controls: Above the system safe area there is a translucent input hint “Add a caption…” on the left. A black/very dark rounded toolbar sits above the system bottom with three touch targets: left circular avatar + label “Your story”; middle rounded black button with green star labeled “Close Friends”; right-most is a circular blue send-arrow floating button with white arrow — this acts as the primary action. The bottom toolbar has about 16–20 px vertical padding and a slight inner shadow to separate from the story.

Typography: Headline — heavy rounded geometric sans (example: Montserrat ExtraBold or Nunito ExtraBold). Approx sizes on a 1080px wide canvas: headline ~96–120 px (scales responsively), line height ~0.9–1.0 to create tight stack. Callout bubble text — medium weight sans (e.g., 16–20 px), line height 1.3–1.5, centered within the bubble. Brand line and small captions — 14–16 px regular. Hydration number — large display number ~48–72 px bold.

Color palette (primary observed + provided):
- Turquoise / Teal: #12BD9D (primary headline, large number, accents)
- Lime / Chartreuse: #BDAB20 (use shown as bright green in stripes and small accent elements)
- Dark / Near-black: #0E0E0E (text and bottom toolbar background)
- Mid Gray: #9A9B9B (icon buttons, muted text)
- Accent Coral: #DC604A (used minimally for small UI or callouts — included as main palette)
- White: #FFFFFF (main background and text bubble fill)
- Light Gray (illustration stripe): #DCE3E8 or #E6E9EB (approx for pale stripe)
- Brown (tail tip): #6E402F or similar dark brown

Iconography & shapes: All UI icons are simple white line/glyph icons inside circular gray (80% brightness) buttons (diameter ~56 px). Drink icons are flat pictograms, evenly sized (~36–44 px). The send action is a filled circular CTA (blue circle ~56 px) with a centered right-pointing arrow glyph.

Spacing & layout metrics (approx on 1080×2400 canvas):
- Safe margins: 24–32 px left/right for main alignment. Headline top margin ~64 px from top safe area. Bubble top margin ~12–18 px under headline. Hero illustration top edge starts ~20–30 px under bubble and extends to just above drink icons. Horizontal centering for main hero.
- Right stacked circular action buttons: 56×56 px circles, 12–18 px vertical spacing, X offset ~12 px from right edge.
- Bottom toolbar height: ~84 px including safe area; internal padding 14–18 px.

States & micro-interactions: Instagram overlays animate in/out with a 160–260 ms ease-out. Circular action buttons highlight on press with a 0.12s scale-down (0.95) and darker background overlay. The send CTA has a subtle rising animation when enabled (translateY -6 px, 200 ms). The hydration number can animate from previous value to new with a short 400 ms count-up easing.

Visual style summary: Flat, playful, highly illustrative social-share design. Uses bright, saturated brand colors (turquoise and lime) against a white negative space background for strong contrast. Typography is rounded and friendly; icons are large and touch-friendly. Instagram native chrome (rounded pills and circular buttons) is preserved and placed as overlays above the content.

Specific actions (element-level):
- Tap the left X to close/dismiss the story composer. (Close button provides immediate dismissal.)
- Tap any right-side circular icon to open that Instagram tool (add text: “Aa”; stickers/emojis; music selection; filters/sparkles; minimize or expand). Buttons show tactile feedback on press.
- Read the congratulatory text inside the speech bubble; it is informational and not interactive (except the avatar may open a profile if tapped in some contexts).
- Inspect hydration summary elements at the bottom (drink icons and the oz counter). The oz number may be tappable to open a detailed hydration log (not shown but implied).
- Tap the “Add a caption…” input to type text (onscreen keyboard appears). The input accepts plain text and supports mention/hashtag/autocomplete via Instagram’s keyboard.
- Choose sharing target by tapping the left “Your story” pill or the center “Close Friends” pill to change destination. These act as toggles (active/inactive) and show selection states.
- Tap the blue circular send-arrow to publish the story to the selected destination.

Medium-level tasks (workflows):
- Compose and annotate a shareable hydration milestone: user reviews the art and message, optionally adds text/stickers/music, previews, and then shares to Story or Close Friends.
- Customize the visual: open text tool to add caption (change size, color), or choose sticker/emojis from the sticker menu; apply music from the music menu; apply sparkles filter.
- Track hydration progress: glance at the drink icons and the oz counter to validate the current hydration level (91 oz). The interface supports quick visual confirmation of progress without leaving the composer.

Broader goals (why user uses this screen):
- Quickly share a hydration achievement/encouragement card to their social network (Instagram Story), promoting consistency and social accountability.
- Use a branded template (Waterllama) to gamify hydration through shareable visuals and a count of ounces consumed. The screen makes it easy to celebrate progress and encourage friends.
- Provide a frictionless composition flow — clear primary CTA (send), accessible editing controls, and immediate feedback — so users can publish a story in a few taps.
